Continue the YM-to-Weil investigation directly in `/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity`. Preserve existing uncommitted work and follow the repository’s instructions and large-file policy.

Start with the project outline and the latest character-channel investigation. Read the earlier source-domain, compact-existence, and pairing-determination notes referenced there as needed.

The objective remains an independently defined, admissible YM source law—or a rigorous source-occurrence theorem—whose actual reflected mixed pairing equals the complete Weil form on the global pole-neutral test space. OS positivity may be assumed. A separately identified native arithmetic translation generator is optional.

The latest note claims that character packets in the fixed interacting SU(2) state satisfy\
[\
\lim\_{R\to\infty}\langle S\_Rf,V\_aS\_Rg\rangle\_\nu\
\=a^{-1/2}\langle f,U\_{\log a}g\rangle,\
]\
and that the operator Euler coefficients produce the full prime-power contribution through a distributional insertion with controlled tails. These claims are provisional research deductions.

First, critically rederive the claims on which further work will depend. Concentrate on the actual weighted adjoints, phase branching, the infinite prime insertion and its domain, and the electric-current limit and its failure on other phase components. Identify and correct substantive errors before using the results. The 57 floating controls are diagnostics, not proofs of the limiting statements.

Then pursue the missing archimedean contribution and its compatibility with positivity. The target off-diagonal kernel is\
[\
-\frac{e^{-|x-y|/2}}{1-e^{-2|x-y|}},\
]\
with the completed Fourier multiplier\
[\
\operatorname{Re}\psi(1/4+i\tau/2)-\log\pi.\
]\
Recovering the kernel alone is insufficient: the local normalization and logarithmic high-frequency growth must also be justified.

Choose at most two concrete candidate mechanisms arising from independently specified YM observables, insertions, or source relations. For each candidate, specify the operator or observable, its domain, the actual state-dependent pairing, and the identities that can be derived. Investigate whether the electric–Wilson current and character operations can supply the missing response while controlling all phase components that winding creates. Do not define an insertion by simply assigning it the desired digamma multiplier.

Address the two established obstacles explicitly:

1. The raw packets converge weakly to zero while retaining norm and violate the existing compact-source bounds. Explain how a proposed source preserves its pairing in the physical representation, or prove why the proposed construction cannot do so.
2. Positive prime squared differences introduce a divergent local coefficient. Any subtraction, constraint, or renormalization must have an independently justified physical definition and a proved positive completed limit. Subtracting the divergence formally does not establish positivity.

Keep the present four-dimensional model and state fixed for the main argument. Use two-dimensional YM or the profinite comparison only when it helps resolve a specific mathematical question. Clearly identify any proposed change of physical model. A nonconstructive occurrence argument is welcome if its hypotheses are independently established.

Aim for a concrete mathematical advance: a proved mixed identity, an admissible source construction, a sufficient occurrence theorem with verified hypotheses, or a precisely scoped obstruction. If a candidate fails, record the reason and pursue the other justified option. Distinguish proofs, conditional statements, conjectures, and numerical evidence throughout. Do not replace the investigation with a bibliography or a collection of positive finite matrices.

Save new analysis in the investigation’s notes directory, substantive audits in reviews, and reproducible numerical controls with small records in numerics. Update the outline and indexes to reflect the actual result. Record the model and reasoning effort when exposed, otherwise mark them unavailable, and acknowledge LLM assistance.

Finish with the strongest established result, its proof assumptions, any corrected earlier claims, the exact remaining mathematical gap, and links to the saved files.

I’ll read the outline and latest character-channel note, audit the claims needed for further work, then develop at most two archimedean candidates. I’ll preserve the existing changes and separate proofs from conditional arguments and numerical diagnostics.

The character metric and branching formula check out so far with the actual marginal density retained. I’m now checking the domain claims and the current on nonzero phases: a finite mixed-pairing limit can survive even when the insertion is not a Hilbert-space vector.

A useful second candidate is emerging: a normalized electric derivative converts the character sine series to a cosine series. Pairing that response with the sum of logarithmic electric scale and logarithmic holonomy angle appears to produce the required digamma term, with its constant fixed by the integer-label/angle Fourier convention. I’ll check the domain and limit carefully; this signed response would still need a separate positivity argument.

The prime obstruction is stronger than the earlier packet calculation: the infinite positive sum \(\sum_a\Lambda(a)\|(I-V_a)F\|^2\) is finite only for \(F=0\) throughout the closed one-plaquette class space. I also found that the phase at \(\pi\) has the opposite current direction, so winding by two fails to preserve the derivative relation even though its current norm stays finite.

The new insertion now gives the full archimedean multiplier in the calculation, including the \(-\log\pi\) constant and logarithmic high-frequency growth. Combined with the prime identities, it yields a complete signed mixed limit. It does not yield a positive source: the response diverges on nonidentity winding phases, and the packets still have no nonzero strong limit. I’m recording those limits and obstructions explicitly in the notes and indexes.

Derived a **complete signed mixed Weil limit** in the fixed SU(2) state. The specified radial electric/angle insertion produces the full digamma multiplier, including its contact normalization and logarithmic growth. The proof uses the smooth positive marginal and explicit operator domains; it remains subject to independent review. [Analysis and proofs](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/YM/notes/ELECTRIC_PARITY_ARCHIMEDEAN_RESPONSE_AND_PHASE_OBSTRUCTION_20260925.md)

The audit retained the core weighted-adjoint, branching, and prime-limit formulas, but clarified distributional admissibility and established two stronger obstructions:

- The phase at \(\pi\) reverses the current, so winding by two also fails the derivative relation.
- The infinite positive prime-difference form has domain only zero throughout the one-plaquette class space.

[Substantive audit](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/YM/reviews/CHARACTER_CURRENT_AND_PRIME_DOMAIN_AUDIT_20260925.md)

**The remaining gap is a positive, admissible source realization.** Neither candidate controls all winding phases, preserves a nonzero strong physical source limit, or supplies a proved positive prime renormalization. The signed identity does not establish Weil positivity.

All 19 new controls and the earlier 57 controls passed; they remain diagnostics. [Reproduction and records](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-loewner/YM/numerics/README.md)
